_comment: ROUND-2 overnight pipeline config (run_training.py): segment-based fetching sweep + adaptive playback + multi-seed evals. Round 1 (DQN_REPORT §9) settled the reward shape — bounded stall won decisively — so it is FIXED in base_args and the new axes are segment size, mu, and the lstm_pred ablation. Commit this file with any change: a run is fully described by repo state.

lstm._signal: achieved = train on per-SEGMENT achieved-throughput series generated by gen_lstm_dataset.py under the current transport model (matches what the predictor is FED at inference); capacity = legacy DL_bitrate training
lstm._gen_args: 8 offsets because segment-level series are short (~30 samples per 300-frame episode at S=10) — more windows keep the sequence count healthy
lstm._sequence_length: 8 (was 20): at S=10 an episode only yields ~30 throughput samples, so seq_len 20 would leave the predictor cold for 2/3 of the episode

dqn_sweep._seeds: TWO training seeds per config (round-1 lesson: single-seed winners can be jitter luck); sweep.py averages metrics across seeds
dqn_sweep._base_args: eval-seeds: every held-out eval averages 3 jitter seeds (kills the one-off-spike checkpoint problem). playback-rate-min 0.9 = research-backed imperceptible slowdown floor. reward-spec fixed to the round-1 winner shape.
dqn_sweep._axes: 6 segment sizes (1 = round-1 control; 30 included deliberately to measure-and-reject the only-10-decisions regime) x 2 mu (stall weight may shift once stalls become rare) x lstm ablation = 24 configs x 2 seeds = 48 trials. Large-S trials are much cheaper (fewer decisions/episode).
